page: Microsoft Azure D8_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering 2 threads per core. Processing power is supplied by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C CPU clocked at 2.8 GHz. The processor architecture includes a 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no local disk storage bundled, relying exclusively on remote persistent disk volumes for storage requirements. In addition, it does not include GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, ensuring baseline compute and memory isolation without dedicated hardware acceleration components.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The virtual machine scored 1532.0 in Geekbench single-core and 5707.0 in multi-core metrics, aligning with its 11506.09 PassMark CPU score and 7750.75 stress-ng multi-core result. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register 50.06 GB/sec for reads and 37.64 GB/sec for writes. In application-oriented tests, the system handled 7.82 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 10.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. A notable limitation is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which placed in the bottom 25% benchmark tier at 27.96 GB/sec.

With its balanced allocation of compute and RAM, the Azure D8_v5 delivers reliable operational efficiency for environments that do not require high-speed ephemeral local disks. Appropriate workload deployments include enterprise web serving, microservice orchestrations, moderate-scale relational databases using network-attached disks, software build pipelines, and general caching servers.

The server provides 32.0 GB of memory, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, but includes neither local disk storage nor GPU accelerators.
